record_type_quote: The purpose of the present study was to identify the reading strategies used by students who are deaf by investigating their self-reported thinking during reading and to compare the results to those found in a previous study, conducted by the lead author of the present article (see Schirmer, 2003), in order to ascertain the reliability of the results.

targets.title: Using verbal protocols to identify reading strategies of students who are deaf.
targets.evidence_quote: The purpose of the present study was to identify the reading strategies used by students who are deaf by investigating their self-reported thinking during reading and to compare the results to those found in a previous study, conducted by the lead author of the present article (see Schirmer, 2003), in order to ascertain the reliability of the results.
targets.outcome_quote: Analysis of these verbal reports indicated the participants performed similarly to those in the first study, thus supporting the reliability of results regarding reading strategies of readers who are deaf.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The abstract gives an overall agreement verdict about the replication. The discussion affirms the reliability of both central findings, despite differences in particular strategy instances.

reasoning: Six new participants re-test the lead author's 2003 published findings. Original protocols are additionally recoded for comparability, but the central attempt uses a new sample and is coded replication. Pressley and Afflerbach is a meta-analysis supplying coding categories, not an independent original target; other studies are literature context. Reference title copied as printed, without adding the article 'the' found in some external citations.
